sets.label: Basic Needs
sets.description: Common requests a patient needs to communicate to caregivers.
sentences: I need water.
I am hungry.
I need to use the bathroom.
Please help me sit up.
Please help me lie down.
I am cold.
I am hot.
Please bring my glasses.
Please bring my phone.
I am ready to sleep.
I need a blanket.
Can you adjust the bed.
Please open the window.
Please close the curtain.
I would like to brush my teeth.
Please bring me a tissue.
I need help getting dressed.
Can someone help me stand up.
I want to make a phone call.
Please turn off the television.

sets.label: Medical Communication
sets.description: Phrases used with doctors, nurses, and therapists.
sentences: I am in pain.
My head hurts.
My chest feels tight.
I feel dizzy.
I cannot breathe well.
Please call the doctor.
When do I take my medicine.
Yes that helps.
No that makes it worse.
Where is the bathroom.
My stomach feels sick.
My back is sore.
My left leg is numb.
My throat hurts when I swallow.
The medicine is making me sleepy.
I have a fever.
I feel weak today.
I had trouble sleeping last night.
I need a glass of water with my pills.
Has the doctor visited this morning.

sets.label: Emotional Expression
sets.description: Sentences that exercise prosody and expressive vocabulary.
sentences: I am happy to see you.
I am scared.
I love you.
I am angry.
I miss my family.
Thank you very much.
I am sorry.
I am tired today.
I feel hopeful.
I do not feel well.
I feel grateful for everything.
I am proud of my progress.
Today was a good day.
I want to go home soon.
Please tell my children I love them.
I am worried about the surgery.
I feel much better than yesterday.
I appreciate your kindness.
I am embarrassed to ask for help.
Some days are harder than others.

sets.label: Phoneme-balanced Sentences
sets.description: TIMIT-style sentences chosen so the combined set covers every English phoneme. Reading these gives the trainer good coverage even with a modest clip count.
sentences: She had your dark suit in greasy wash water all year.
Don't ask me to carry an oily rag like that.
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs.
Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow.
Two driven jocks help fax my big quiz.
How quickly daft jumping zebras vex.
The five boxing wizards jump quickly.
Bright vixens jump; dozy fowl quack.
Glib jocks quiz nymph to vex dwarf.
Jackdaws love my big sphinx of quartz.
Cozy lummox gives smart squid who asks for job pen.
A wizard's job is to vex chumps quickly in fog.
Watch Jeopardy alex Trebek's fun TV quiz game.
Crazy Fredrick bought many very exquisite opal jewels.
Few thoughts arise during my brief calm sleep.
Many roads have splendid views in the morning fog.
Bring sturdy yellow umbrellas when the weather turns.
Children playfully chased the noisy ducks across the pond.
Eleven musicians performed jazz songs beside the bonfire.
Cathy was charging the phone with the new red cord.
Soft music plays in the background of the doctor's office.
The therapist asked her to count slowly from one to ten.
We saved a place near the window for grandfather to sit.
Yesterday I drank a tall glass of lemonade in the shade.

sets.label: Phoneme Drills
sets.description: Short minimal-pair and stress-pattern drills that exercise consonants the patient adapter struggles with most. Quick reps, low cognitive load.
sentences: Red lorry, yellow lorry, red lorry, yellow lorry.
Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.
She sells seashells by the seashore.
How much wood would a woodchuck chuck.
Around the rugged rock the ragged rascal ran.
A proper copper coffee pot.
Toy boat, toy boat, toy boat.
Unique New York, unique New York.
Black bug bit a big black bear.
Six slick slim slender saplings.
Truly rural, truly rural, truly rural.
Eleven benevolent elephants.
Greek grapes, Greek grapes, Greek grapes.
Irish wristwatch, Swiss wristwatch.
Mixed biscuits, mixed biscuits, mixed biscuits.
Pad kid poured curd pulled cold.
Fresh french fried fish.
Lesser leather never weathered wetter weather.
Sheep should sleep in a shed.
Three free throws.

sets.label: Conversational
sets.description: Natural everyday sentences with broad coverage of common function words and contractions, which is where ASR usually pays off most.
sentences: What time is dinner today.
Could you turn the heat up a little.
I'd like to call my daughter later.
Do you remember where you put my book.
I'm not sure I understood what you said.
It was raining when I woke up this morning.
Can we walk in the garden after lunch.
I'll try to do that exercise again tomorrow.
She brought the photo album from the closet.
He hasn't answered the phone all afternoon.
We watched the news together last night.
There's a new nurse on the evening shift.
I always took the long way home from school.
I'd rather rest now and try again later.
Did the physical therapist say when I can stand.
I keep forgetting what day of the week it is.
The window faces east so the sun wakes me early.
My grandson visited me on Saturday afternoon.
The coffee tastes much better this morning.
Could you read that letter out loud one more time.
I haven't been outside in three days.
I'm hoping the rain stops by the weekend.
The hospital food is better than I expected.
Tell me again about the trip you took last summer.
I keep thinking about that song from when I was young.

sets.label: Numbers and Dates
sets.description: Number and date pronunciations are an outsized share of medical communication failures (medication times, room numbers). Worth giving the adapter explicit coverage.
sentences: Today is the fifteenth of November.
My next appointment is at three forty-five.
I take two pills every six hours.
Room four oh seven.
I was born in nineteen forty-two.
It's been nineteen days since the surgery.
I take one tablet of the white pill at eight in the morning.
I weigh one hundred and sixty pounds.
Please call my son, his number is four one five, five five five, zero one two seven.
I take the smaller pill at noon and the larger one at six in the evening.
It is now seventeen minutes past two.
My birthday is on October the third.
The dose is twenty-five milligrams, twice a day.
We have lived at this address for thirty-one years.
The thermostat should stay around seventy-two degrees.
